anomalies.observed: The single net named "SCK" carries the shared SPI clock of the three MAX31855s AND the USB D+ line: it contains U1 pin 19 (GPIO5/ADC2_CH0), U1 pin 27 (GPIO19/USB_D+), J12 pins A6/B6 (USB-C D+) and U2/U3/U4 pin 5 (SCK). The SPI clock is therefore shorted to the USB D+ data line and to the ESP32's native USB pin.
anomalies.expected: The SPI clock net should connect only the ESP32 SPI clock pin and the three thermocouple SCK inputs. Per the spec the bus is on GPIO5 only, and the USB D+ line should connect only U1 GPIO19/USB_D+ to J12 D+. The two signals must be separate nets.

evidence.quote: SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7

anomalies.impact: The USB D+ line is bridged with the SPI clock (and with GPIO5/GPIO19). Every thermocouple read toggles SCK and corrupts the USB D+ line, and the USB-C connector plus the native USB pin load the SPI clock. USB programming/serial and reliable thermocouple communication cannot coexist; the board will not behave as the intended controller.

anomalies.observed: J5 is a 2-pin screw terminal whose pin 1 is on GND and whose pin 2 is on the "/Microcontroller/HEATER" net, i.e. the ESP32 GPIO1 / U6 IN+DIAG_EN logic control net. It is not connected to the switched heater output (U6 pin 7 OUT, which only reaches J6 pin 2 via Net-(J6-Pin_2)).
anomalies.expected: A screw terminal on this board is a field-wiring connector (thermocouple terminals J1-J3, heater terminal J6, fan headers J7/J8). If J5 is a second heater/aux output it should be tied to the switched output (U6 OUT / J6 pin 2), not to a bare 3.3V MCU GPIO; the spec's heater connector is J6 and it never lists J5 on the HEATER net.

evidence.quote: OUT (pin 7) feeds the heater connector J6 pin 2

anomalies.impact: Wiring a load to J5 would apply the load voltage directly to GPIO1 (destroying the MCU), and even shorting J5's two pins shorts GPIO1 to GND. Field wiring is exposed to a 3.3V logic pin rather than to the protected switched output.

parsed.summary: The design contains a clear connectivity anomaly: the SPI clock net "SCK" is bridged with the USB D+ line (U1 GPIO19/USB_D+, J12 A6/B6) so the shared thermocouple SPI bus is shorted to USB data, contradicting the spec's GPIO5-only SCK. A second, lower-confidence issue is screw terminal J5 being wired to the GPIO1 heater-control net instead of the switched heater output.
